tool_args.rationale: The source-based hydraulic curve nearly matches the low-gradient rows, while the stronger-gradient rows show an additional loss that increases with normalized input. Multiplying two smooth gates captures that pattern: with a representative gradient-gate slope of 15, the model gives about 0.002 training RMSE and 0.012 leave-one-out RMSE, below the 0.045 tolerance. Submit the weakly regularized fit for fresh confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Hydraulic baseline with freely fitted gradient suppression
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: It can fit within the training tolerance, but its residuals are structured. A gradient-only correction still misses the dependence of siphon strength on input.
The observations do not pin down a discontinuity or a precise transition width. Weak regularization keeps the fitted transition smooth without forcing a hard cutoff between observed gradients.
Haldane ignores the observed gradient effect; Cobb–Douglas lacks both input saturation and a branch that can activate jointly with input and gradient.
The two relevant probes have already been acquired at the target horizon. The remaining nuisance measurement does not separate the mechanisms.
